name: Bamburgh & Alnwick Castle Day Trip from Edinburgh
tagline: Explore Bamburgh's seaside fortress, then spend the afternoon at Alnwick Castle — Hogwarts in the Harry Potter films — on a small-group day trip from Edinburgh.
overview:
Run by Haggis Adventures as a small-group day trip, this tour crosses the border into Northumberland for two of its most famous castles. Bamburgh Castle rises from a basalt crag above the North Sea and was the ancient capital of the Northumbrian kingdom — the seaside village below it is one of the most photographed spots on the English coast. The afternoon is spent at Alnwick Castle, the real-life Hogwarts of the Harry Potter films, where travelers can sign up for broomstick lessons on the same lawn used for the films' flying scenes. A live English-speaking guide travels with the group, and downloadable audio guides are included in French, English, German, Italian, Chinese, Portuguese and Spanish.

Prefer Holy Island and Lindisfarne instead of Bamburgh? See the [Holy Island & Alnwick Castle Day Trip from Edinburgh](/tours/scotland/edinburgh-holy-island-alnwick-castle). For a private-vehicle alternative departing from Northumberland itself, with a stop at Chillingham Castle, see [Chillingham, Bamburgh & Alnwick: Private Tour from Northumberland](/tours/england/northumberland-bamburgh-chillingham-alnwick).
highlights: Sign up for broomstick lessons at the real-life Hogwarts
Discover the charming seaside village of Bamburgh
Travel back in time with stories of Scottish and English history
Small-group format with a live English-speaking guide
Downloadable audio guides included in seven languages

itinerary.description: Depart from Haggis Adventures in Edinburgh for the coach journey south into Northumberland.
Free time in the seaside village of Bamburgh, with an optional, separately paid visit to Bamburgh Castle itself, rising from its basalt crag above the North Sea.
Free time to explore Alnwick Castle, with an optional, separately paid entry — the real-life Hogwarts of the Harry Potter films, where the broomstick flying lessons were filmed.
Break in a traditional Northumbrian village for photos before the journey back to Edinburgh.
Return coach journey to Edinburgh, arriving back at Haggis Adventures.

excluded: Entry tickets to Bamburgh and Alnwick Castles (pay on site)
meeting_point: Haggis Adventures, 60 High St, Edinburgh EH1 1TB — same return point
tips: Not suitable for children under 5 or for wheelchair users.
Bring a passport or ID, comfortable shoes, a camera, and weather-appropriate clothing.
Arrive at least 15 minutes early for check-in — late arrivals are not entitled to a refund.
Itinerary order may change. Travel insurance is recommended.
Not allowed: smoking in the vehicle, alcohol or drugs, unaccompanied minors.
Free cancellation up to 24 hours before the tour, with the option to reserve now and pay later.

Planning a summer trip, for example around the Edinburgh Military Tattoo in August? Book early — this tour is flagged as likely to sell out, and free cancellation up to 24 hours lets you lock in a date without risk.
Past travelers consistently praise the guides as engaging and knowledgeable and highlight the scenic stops along the way; some wish for more free time at Bamburgh, particularly to reach the beach.

faqs.question: Can I enter Bamburgh and Alnwick Castles on this tour?
faqs.answer: Entry to both castles is optional and paid on site — the tour itself covers transportation, the guide and free time at each stop, not the entrance tickets.

faqs.question: Which Harry Potter scenes were filmed at Alnwick Castle?
faqs.answer: Alnwick Castle's outer bailey was used for the broomstick flying lesson in Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone — travelers can take their own broomstick lesson on the same lawn.

faqs.question: Does this tour also stop at Holy Island (Lindisfarne)?
faqs.answer: No — this tour visits Bamburgh and Alnwick Castle only. For a tour that includes Holy Island instead of Bamburgh, see our [Holy Island & Alnwick Castle Day Trip from Edinburgh](/tours/scotland/edinburgh-holy-island-alnwick-castle).
